title: 8-foot Sasquatch sculpture coming to Portland as part of Geek Week PDX
excerpt: This will be Geek Week’s first Sasquatch scavenger hunt, but “Chief Goblin Wrangler” David Raycroft revealed it likely won’t be the last.
content:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) — Look out, Portlanders. Bigfoot — or Bigfeet — are coming to town.

An 8-foot Sasquatch sculpture will be unveiled at Portland City Hall in just a few days. It will be one of dozens of pieces of varying sizes spread throughout the city as part of Geek Week PDX’s Sneaky Sasquatch PDX Art Hunt.

Geek Week annually celebrates the “wonderfully nerdy” Rose City, according to the event’s “Chief Goblin Wrangler” David Raycroft. But whereas the festivities typically include costume parties, trivia nights and gaming tournaments, the Bigfoot scavenger hunt is a first for organizers.

Raycroft told KOIN 6 the idea was proposed by a group of artists. Since then, 31 of them have created their own original interpretations of Sasquatch — with the smallest measuring at just two inches tall.

Although the largest sculpture will be unveiled downtown on Sept. 8, the search for the others will span throughout Geek Week from Sept. 11 to Sept. 20. Organizers have already released clues to have participants find each piece.

“They’re placed throughout the city in small businesses, community centers [and] public spaces like parks,” Raycroft said. “It’s just a fun way to really demonstrate and show off the naturally creative culture that is such at the heart of Portland. The thing that makes it a little different is there is no corporate backer. It is just artists donating their time and materials and locations donating their space to inspire the community to get out and find Bigfoot.”

The largest piece was created by Moni Sears and Rick Sears, according to Raycroft. The duo known as Goblin Art has also had their work featured as part of events like the Portland Winter Light Festival and in films like “The Wicker Man.”

Raycroft noted that a majority of Geek Week festivities, including the Sasquatch hunt, will be free.
